trust_decision.summary: wsRecv decides, before any auth check, when an unauthenticated request is complete by adding an attacker-supplied Content-Length (parsed as usize) to header_end+4 with checked arithmetic; overflow panics the plugin thread/process.

landing_point.why: The only place Content-Length is used in arithmetic; parseContentLength (mcp_server.zig:917) is in the same file and named by the summary.

fix_sites.entry_point: any TCP/HTTP request to the MCP listener (handleClient -> wsRecv), pre-auth
server start with no config (default bind address), hardening not part of the overflow
setConfig with empty ip (default bind address), hardening
GET / server info, version string only (cosmetic)
About menu dialog, version string only (cosmetic)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No other route exists; the bind-address change is a hardening default, not a second site of the overflow.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests whose body arrives in several recv() chunks must still be read until header_end+4+Content-Length bytes; requests with no/zero Content-Length must return immediately. Rejecting large or capping lengths too aggressively breaks normal tools/call POSTs.

O6_input_shapes: Content-Length near usize max (decimal digits only, 'Content-Length: ' or 'content-length: ' spelling per mcp_server.zig:918-920)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a POST body slice computed as request[header_end + 4 .. header_end + 4 + content_length] honouring Content-Length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer trimming trailing bytes to the declared body length would naturally reuse parseContentLength here; it is the same arithmetic on the same field.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a case-insensitive Content-Length lookup via parseHeaderValue with its own parseInt and addition
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseContentLength only matches two spellings; a fix for 'Content-length:' would plausibly add a second parser, giving a parser-differential copy.

O9_family: integer overflow (CWE-190) in HTTP Content-Length arithmetic leading to panic / pre-auth crash

O10_build.toolchain: zig build (version per build.zig.zon), cross-compiles to Windows DLL plugins .dp32/.dp64 only
services: x64dbg host process (Windows GUI debugger) to load the plugin
O10_build.project_tests: none; build.zig defines no test step and the repo contains no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Use saturating/checked addition (or cap Content-Length at buffer size) at mcp_server.zig:431, which is also the complete fix.

out_of_scope_notes: wsRecv has no recv timeout and each connection gets its own thread (mcp_server.zig:395, 423-427): slow-client resource exhaustion, not pursued.
Default bind 0.0.0.0 with CORS '*' (mcp_server.zig:58, 845) is a separate exposure hardened in the same commit.
unverified: repo_mb not measured; only a handful of source files plus PNGs, clearly under 5 MB.
Whether released binaries are built with ReleaseSafe/Debug (panic) or ReleaseFast (wrap); build.zig:4 uses standardOptimizeOption so it depends on the release build command.
The plugin is a Windows DLL loaded by x64dbg (src/core/bridge.zig); running it headless under Linux was not checked.
